report:
Based on the evidence gathered, here is my conclusion.

**Conclusion:** Yes — dexamethasone and similar corticosteroids reduce mortality among critically ill (severely hypoxic or mechanically ventilated) COVID-19 patients, though the benefit is not universal to all COVID-19 patients, only those with more severe disease.

The landmark UK RECOVERY trial, a large randomized controlled trial, found that dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality by about one-third in patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and by about one-fifth in patients requiring supplemental oxygen alone (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/opinion-any-scientific-matter/dexamethasone-covid19-article-53-procedure-assessment-report_en.pdf; https://www.livescience.com/dexamethasone-covid19-trial-early-results.html).

This finding was corroborated by the WHO's prospective meta-analysis (REACT Working Group), which pooled data from seven randomized trials of over 1,700 critically ill patients and found that systemic corticosteroids were associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality compared with usual care or placebo (https://www.pulmccm.org/p/more-on-corticosteroids-in-covid-19-part-2-react-meta-analysis).

Subsequent independent meta-analyses have generally reinforced this conclusion, showing reduced mortality in "severe" and "critical" COVID-19 patients, with survival benefit particularly clear at low-to-moderate doses given for about 7–10 days (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567576921007578; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8413363/).

**Important caveats:** The benefit is confined to patients with significant hypoxia/severe disease requiring oxygen or ventilation. In patients with mild disease or no oxygen requirement, corticosteroids show no mortality benefit and may even be harmful (potentially prolonging viral shedding or increasing secondary infection risk). At least one meta-analysis found the mortality benefit was not statistically convincing when analyses excluded the RECOVERY trial or used different corticosteroid regimens (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500308/), underscoring some heterogeneity in results depending on dose, timing, and steroid type. Overall, current evidence strongly supports corticosteroid use specifically in oxygen-dependent, critically ill COVID-19 patients.
